# Scientific method and limitations

BlinkSpace shows real SPHEREx Level-2 spectral images of one sky position at different times, and nothing else.
This document states exactly what the pipeline does to the data, why, and where it stops being trustworthy.
Every rule below is enforced by a test in `backend/tests` (file names in brackets).

## 1. What a SPHEREx "image at a wavelength" is

Each SPHEREx detector sits behind a linear variable filter: the central wavelength changes continuously across the
detector. A star is therefore observed at a different wavelength in every exposure, depending on where it lands.
**The same detector does not mean the same wavelength** [`test_science.py::test_same_detector_does_not_mean_same_wavelength`].

Consequences for a time comparison:

- Two frames may be compared in time only if the wavelength *at the target* is the same. BlinkSpace requires
  `|λ − λ_ref| ≤ tol × Δλ`, with Δλ the bandwidth (FWHM) at λ_ref. Default `tol = 0.5` (centres at most half a
  resolution element apart: adequate for visual inspection). Quantitative brightness comparison uses `tol = 0.25`;
  if fewer than two/three points satisfy it, the 0.5 set is used with an added 10% systematic for the spectral
  slope, and this is stated in the result.
- The match at the centre does not hold across the field: the wavelength gradient is about one resolution element
  per ~180 detector pixels. A per-pixel wavelength map is computed for every frame, and pixels outside the tolerance
  are masked as "not comparable" (blue layer in the viewer) [`test_wavelength_map_and_comparable_mask`].
- Frames at other wavelengths are offered separately as "wavelength exploration" and as a spectrum; they are never
  placed in a time sequence.

Wavelengths come from the `WCS-WAVE` lookup table inside each file (bilinear interpolation, ~1 nm accuracy per the
archive documentation). Our evaluation is checked against astropy's `-TAB` implementation on real files (identical
to 1e-9 µm) [`test_live_archive.py`]. The SIP distortion must not be applied to the alternate "A"/"W" coordinate
systems; astropy applies it by default, which shifted detector coordinates by ~24 pixels in our first reading.

## 2. Finding and selecting observations

- One TAP query (`spherex.plane ⨝ spherex.artifact`, `CONTAINS(POINT, poly)`) returns every Level-2 image whose
  footprint contains the position. Times are UTC (MJD).
- A record is one exposure × one detector. Reprocessed copies of the same (observation id, detector) are **one**
  observation: the newest release/L2 version/processing date is kept. Different detectors stay separate
  [`test_reprocessed_copies_are_one_observation_and_detectors_stay_separate`].
- Before downloading, the target's detector pixel is estimated from the four footprint corners (measured accuracy on
  real files: 3–8 pixels) and its wavelength from a per-detector `WCS-WAVE` table. Exposures with the target too
  close to the detector edge for the requested field are dropped.
- Candidates are grouped by wavelength; the default group is the one with the most separate visits, then the longest
  time span. Up to N frames are chosen, one per visit first, keeping the first and last visit.
- After download the wavelength is recomputed from the file itself and the tolerance re-applied; a frame that fails
  is rejected and listed.

## 3. Reading the files

HDUs are read **by name**. Verified on real files: QR2 (pipeline 6.4, 6.5.x) has `PSF` as the fifth HDU, pipeline
7.0.x has `EPSF`. Flag definitions are read from each file's `FLAGS` header (`MP_<NAME>` in 6.x, `MSKNnnnn` in 7.x);
no fixed bit table is assumed [`test_reads_both_release_layouts_by_name`, `test_flag_definitions_come_from_each_file_header`].

Flag classes:

| Class | Flags | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| invalid | NONFUNC, MISSING_DATA, SUR_ERROR, HOT, COLD, PHANTOM, REFERENCE, non-finite values | no measurement: NaN, transparent in previews, never zero |
| suspect | TRANSIENT, OVERFLOW, NONLINEAR, PERSIST, OUTLIER, PHANMISS, DICHROIC, FULLSAMPLE, CROSSTALK, GHOST*, STREAK, BLOOM, SNOWBALL, HALO, and any unknown new name | value shown, mask carried separately |
| info | SOURCE | no mask |

## 4. Alignment

All frames are resampled (bilinear, `reproject`) onto one grid: tangent projection centred on the requested ICRS
position, north up, east left, native 6.15″ pixels, odd size. Alignment uses only each file's own WCS (TAN-SIP).
**No source is pinned between frames**, so real motion survives [`test_controlled_shift_is_measured_and_moving_source_is_not_pinned`].

- Invalid pixels are set to NaN before resampling; the invalid mask is resampled as a float and any output pixel it
  touches is invalid (conservative growth). Suspect masks are carried by nearest neighbour. Flag bits are never
  interpolated [`test_invalid_pixels_stay_missing_not_zero_and_flags_are_not_averaged`].
- Coverage outside a frame's footprint is invalid; frames covering < 60% of the grid are rejected.
- **Check:** for every sequence, Gaia DR3 stars (G ≤ 15.5, isolated, clean) are propagated to each frame epoch and
  their centroids measured in the aligned frame. Residual rms on the five targets: 0.4–1.3″ (0.06–0.2 pixel), except
  R Dra where stars inside the saturated star's halo dominate (reported as measured).

## 5. Background and display

Per frame, a sigma-clipped median of valid, unflagged, non-source pixels is subtracted (constant; value and scatter
recorded per frame; the archive's ZODI model median is recorded too but not used). All frames of a sequence share one
asinh stretch and one black/white pair. Previews are 8-bit PNGs with transparent invalid pixels and are **never** used
for measurement.

## 6. Measurements

- **Position:** flux-weighted centroid in a 5×5 box on the aligned frame. Per-point error = the sequence's own Gaia
  residual rms (floor 0.1 pixel). For a saturated star the centroid of the invalid core is used with an assumed
  0.3-pixel error.
- **Motion:** linear fit of position against time; compared with the catalogue proper motion. Parallax and
  spacecraft position are not modelled (≤ 0.55″ for these targets, < 0.1 pixel). The predicted-position overlay is
  proper-motion-only and labelled so.
- **Brightness:** aperture photometry (r = 2 pixels, annulus 4–7) on the **native, un-resampled** cutout with the
  VARIANCE layer. Any invalid pixel in the aperture → no measurement. OVERFLOW/NONLINEAR in the aperture → value
  kept but marked unreliable. No aperture correction: only relative changes at one wavelength are meaningful.
  Comparison stars (Gaia, same frames, same aperture) give a per-frame scale and a systematic scatter that is added
  to the errors.
- **"Change seen"** = ≥ 3σ in our own measurement (brightness additionally ≥ 20% and normalised by comparison
  stars). It is never reported as scientifically confirmed.

## 7. Advanced products and their limits

| Product | What it is | Limits |
|---|---|---|
| Difference | B − A of background-subtracted, wavelength-comparable valid pixels | no PSF matching; undersampled PSF leaves residuals on static stars; PSF FWHM differs between releases (5.3″ vs 7.5″) |
| Stack | mean of valid comparable pixels, ≥ max(2, n/2) frames per pixel | moving sources blur (expected motion in pixels is shown); variable sources are averaged |
| Gaia / AllWISE layers | **catalogue** positions (not images) | Gaia epoch 2016.0, propagated by proper motion; AllWISE ≈ 2010.5, not propagated; resolutions differ |
| Light curve | aperture flux vs real date for one wavelength group | see Brightness above |
| Spectrum | aperture flux vs wavelength from all exposures in a time window | **not simultaneous**; each point carries its date; blended neighbours within 12″ |
| Candidate suggestions | ≥ 6σ regions of the difference image whose 5×5 box flux changes by ≥ 25%; ± pair within 4 px = possible motion; touching flagged pixels = possible artefact | review aid only; validated on synthetic injections (labelled as such in the tests), not a detection pipeline |

## 8. Known limitations

- Pixel scale 6.15″ and an undersampled PSF: close pairs (Eps Indi Ba/Bb, RW Aur A/B) are one source; background
  stars within ~12″ contaminate photometry (this is what prevents a clean WISE 0855 measurement).
- Bright stars saturate: Barnard's Star, R Dra and RW Aur longward of ~0.85 µm have invalid or unreliable cores.
- Quick-release / first-release calibration; aperture fluxes are not absolute.
- The Gaia query for the alignment check adds 30–85 s for a new position.
- No shift-and-stack along a predicted motion, no PSF photometry, no PSF-matched differencing.
- Synthetic data are used only in automated tests (`conftest.py::FakeArchive`), never in the app or the reports.

# Motion model

## model

The 3D scenes propagate catalogue astrometry as a Cartesian ICRS position and a constant
space velocity between 2000 and 2100. Right ascension proper motion includes cos(declination).
The Three.js presentation uses the coordinate order (ICRS x, ICRS z, ICRS y), with +Y north.
One neighbourhood unit is one parsec. Missing radial velocity is represented by an explicit
zero-velocity assumption; it is not a measured zero. Annual parallax, spacecraft viewpoint
and orbital motion are not included in this catalogue space-motion model.

The stellar surface and limb darkening are representative. Its colour follows a
temperature-labelled blackbody calculation when a temperature exists. A source-cited
radius can parameterize a compressed visual scale, but the drawn diameter is not an
angular-size measurement. A cool infrared source can be nearly invisible in visible
light. Neither the texture nor its surrounding animation is a resolved SPHEREx image.

SPHEREx time stacks contain the real, individually dated image planes. The planes do not
interpolate or animate the image pixels. A line through predicted catalogue positions is a
computed guide. Measured centroids are separate and can be missing, saturated or blended.
The co-moving stack is a display product, not photometry; static sources become smeared.

Sources: the application's source-labelled catalogue and reference constants, `SPEC.md`
rules 7–10, `docs/METHOD.md`, and the motion golden tests. Numerical results must be taken
from the current catalogue/context or a dated report, not inferred from this description.

## source-labelled-stellar-models

The five curated profiles served at `/api/models` cite their parameter sources and mark
measured, computed, representative or assumed values. Missing radius or temperature
values stay missing. The interface exposes the source parameters separately from the
drawing. The resource is `backend/blinkspace/resources/stellar_profiles.json`.

Barnard's Star has a representative active M-dwarf environment. Epsilon Indi B contains
two T-dwarf components; the display can illustrate a binary orbit without claiming a
measured orbital phase or sky orientation. WISE 0855 uses a cool Y-dwarf atmosphere
representation. RW Aurigae includes a schematic disk, jets and dust obscuration. R Draconis
includes illustrative pulsation and dust outflow. A sourced pulsation period does not
establish the displayed phase, angular radius or outflow geometry.

These environment animations explain source-supported phenomena. Particle trajectories,
texture patterns, apparent separations and animation speeds are representative unless
a specific displayed quantity has an explicit source and epistemic label. They are not
time-resolved images or hydrodynamic simulations.
# Epistemic labels

## labels

- **Measured / ölçülen:** an observed catalogue value or a measurement on valid image data;
  include its unit, source and uncertainty when available. The UI uses white.
- **Computed / hesaplanan:** a result calculated from cited inputs, for example distance
  from parallax or a predicted position at a chosen year. The UI uses orange.
- **Representative / temsili:** a graphic chosen to explain the data, such as the enlarged
  stellar surface or the spacing of time-stack planes. Its size is not a measurement;
  use a label and a dashed boundary.
- **Assumed / varsayılan:** an explicit modelling choice when an input is unavailable,
  for example radial velocity set to zero for propagation. Use an underlined label.

These categories do not represent confidence scores. A computed result can depend on an
assumption. Missing values remain missing; they must not be silently replaced with zeros.
User marks are unverified observations, not catalogue measurements or discoveries.

# Stellar surfaces and surroundings

The five target models use the cited parameters in `backend/blinkspace/resources/stellar_profiles.json`, served by `/api/models`. Each parameter retains its unit, uncertainty or range where supplied, evidence class, source and limitations. The interface shows these in English and Turkish. Unknown radius or temperature remains unknown.

| Target | Displayed structure | Evidence and limits |
|---|---|---|
| Barnard's Star | Granulated photosphere, coronal shell, magnetic arches and radial wind tracers | Radius 0.187 ± 0.001 R☉, temperature 3195 ± 28 K from the [2024 ESPRESSO study](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.00569v1). [Chandra/Hubble observations](https://www.chandra.si.edu/photo/2020/barnards/index.html) support magnetic activity; the drawn shell and wind are qualitative. No measured field map, wind speed, flare event or planet is invented. |
| Epsilon Indi Ba/Bb | Two separate surfaces, layered advecting clouds and illustrative orbit | 1320 K and 910 K are display midpoints of [BT-Settl model ranges](https://arxiv.org/abs/0911.3143), not new measurements. Each atmosphere follows its own component. The eccentricity and inclination use the [published orbit](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2205.08077); phase, display separation, equal component size and symmetric placement are illustrative. SPHEREx does not resolve the two components. |
| WISE 0855 | Very dark surface, representative cloud bands and thin atmosphere | The adopted 250 K historical reference and later model-dependent analyses are linked in the profile. Visible emission is negligible. The renderer deliberately uses a dark placeholder, not a visible-light photograph or a measured infrared surface map. No physical radius is adopted. |
| RW Aurigae | Flared accretion disk, funnel flows onto the star, differential disk flow, dust contrast and two jet tracer streams | The cited stellar and ALMA measurements describe RW Aur A. [GHOsT spectroscopy](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.10392) constrains gas in its jet. The drawing illustrates A; SPHEREx blends A and B. Star, disk and jet display scales differ. Particle speeds and densities are not inferred measurements. |
| R Draconis | Large convection cells, irregular molecular layers, a radius/temperature/colour cycle and extended outflow | The 511 ± 142 R☉ and 2034 ± 139 K values are [historical, phase-specific K-band estimates](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0210167), not a current photospheric radius or cycle average. GCVS supplies the 245.6-day period. Outflow is a class illustration, not a measured dust quantity. The SPHEREx sequence is saturated. |

## Display choices

- Physical radii, when adopted, use `sqrt(R/R☉)` display units, with a solar reference in the context view. Close-up framing excludes that reference. Unknown single radii use one representative unit; the two unknown binary radii use 0.55 units each. These are separate from the astrometric trail's ×600 scale.
- Photospheric colour uses the existing Planck/CIE/Wyman calculation. Unknown temperatures use a neutral colour. Below 1000 K, the clamped colour is strongly dimmed and explicitly labelled as emitting almost no visible light.
- Eddington limb darkening gives surface depth. Convection cells, cloud bands, accretion polar structure and disk density patterns are procedural, representative structure, not telescope imagery.
- The Mira cycle uses a deliberately illustrative ±5.5% display-radius variation and ±4% temperature excursion. The contraction/heating phase, eight-second cycle and display intensity are not fitted to the SPHEREx light curve. Colours interpolate precomputed blackbody endpoints to avoid an unbounded per-frame temperature cache.
- Disk angular flow decreases with radius as `r^-3/2`; radial wind and bipolar jet particles show direction. Their dimensions, speed and density do not form a fluid or magnetohydrodynamic solution.
- The calendar controls the catalogue's linear space motion. It does not evolve a star's age or predict its future surface. The separate illustrative animation clock advances only with the Surface & flow animation control. It is independent of calendar playback. Pause and reduced-motion preference freeze that clock.
- Surroundings can be hidden without hiding the photosphere or motion trail. A target change disposes its prior disk, atmosphere, jets and secondary component.

## Reusable Three.js models

The live scene now uses five named model recipes through `createStellarModel` in
`frontend/src/three/models/StellarModel.ts`. The same factory exports five `.three.json`
assets in `frontend/public/models/`. The selected target's measurement panel has a
localized model-download link. Each asset contains geometry, procedural materials,
embedded halo texture, adopted parameters, sources, caveats and animation metadata.

`animate-stellar-model.js` updates an ObjectLoader-loaded model with the same animation
code as the live scene. `faceStellarModel` keeps reference circles camera-facing and
caps particle pixel scaling at two. `display_extent` includes vertex-shader outflow;
a static geometry bounding box alone would miss those particles. The model pack README
includes integration instructions. This is the pinned r170 ObjectLoader format, not GLB.

Barnard's added arches use a dipole-like geometric construction. Its magnetic topology
is unknown: even the cited [Barnard wind study](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.00219) uses
proxy magnetic maps. The new arcs are not measured lines or a claim about particular
flares. RW Aur's funnel paths, disk thickness and corrugations are class illustrations;
all disk, funnel and jet structures share one local orientation. The cited disk angle
does not measure the field map. Brown-dwarf cloud opacity and Mira envelope clumping
are also schematic. None of these new structures changes measured SPHEREx pixels.

`npm run models:export` produces deterministic scene identifiers and file hashes, checks
all position values are finite, and parses all five results through ObjectLoader. It
exports reduced geometry while retaining the full procedural materials. The live app
continues to use its selected geometry-quality setting. `npm run build` regenerates the
assets automatically; the build has no archive or model-provider dependency.

## Verification

`frontend/src/tests/stellarModels.test.ts` exercises the actual delivered profiles and motion catalogue: unknown values, class selection, compressed radii, Kepler extrema, wide/narrow camera fitting, binary atmosphere attachment, resource disposal, layer isolation, pause, reduced motion and idle update termination. Two UI tests verify uncertainty, source limitations, component temperatures and Turkish formatting. These are numerical/component checks, not a GPU or visual acceptance test.

The profile builder is reproducible with `PYTHONPATH=backend python -m tools.build_stellar_profiles`. Backend tests reject uncited measurements, promoted unknown values and a false stellar-evolution clock. The fetched GCVS response is bundled with its SHA-256 and parsed period.
